> **What you will build:** A company of 5 autonomous AI agents — Henry, Coder, Scout, Writer, and Watcher — running 24/7 on your own cloud server. You control them by sending text or voice messages through Telegram, from your phone or desktop. They autonomously research, write code, analyze data, produce reports, and monitor your system — around the clock, without your involvement once deployed.

> **What is new in v0.78:** All 5 agents now have Telegram bots (Watcher previously had none). The monitoring dashboard is now publicly accessible at `http://YOUR_IP:8050` — no SSH tunnel required. Dashboard deployment is automated in the deploy script.

---

# Part 1: Create Your DigitalOcean Droplet

## Create a DigitalOcean Account

1. Go to [digitalocean.com](https://www.digitalocean.com) and sign up. Your university email is fine.
2. Add a payment method. The smallest useful droplet costs **\$6/month**.
3. If you have a referral link from the course, use it — new accounts receive \$200 in free credits valid for 60 days, which covers the entire project.

## Create a Droplet

1. Log in and click **Create → Droplets** in the top navigation bar.
2. Configure your droplet with the following settings:

| Setting | Value |
|---------|-------|
| **Region** | Closest to you — New York, San Francisco, Chicago, or Toronto |
| **Image** | Ubuntu 24.04 (LTS) x64 |
| **Size** | Basic → Regular → **\$6/mo** (1 GB RAM, 1 vCPU, 25 GB SSD) |
| **Authentication** | Password — set a strong root password and write it down |
| **Hostname** | `clawinc` (lowercase, no spaces) |

3. Click **Create Droplet**. The server boots in about 60 seconds.
4. Find your droplet's **IP address** in the DigitalOcean dashboard (a number like `143.198.57.112`). You will use this IP address in many places throughout this guide.

> **Write down your IP address now.** You will type it often.

## Connect to Your Droplet via SSH

You will manage your server through a terminal (SSH). Options by platform:

- **Windows:** Use Windows Terminal (`Win + X → Terminal`) or install [PuTTY](https://putty.org). Both support `ssh`.
- **Mac/Linux:** Open the built-in Terminal application.
- **Browser:** In DigitalOcean, click your droplet name → **Access → Launch Droplet Console**.

Open a terminal and connect:

```bash
ssh root@YOUR_DROPLET_IP
# Type your root password when prompted (characters will not appear — that is normal)
```

You should see a prompt like `root@clawinc:~#`. You are now inside your server. Every command in Part 4 and beyond runs here unless otherwise noted.

---

# Part 2: Create Your Telegram Bots (5 Bots)

You need **5 Telegram bots** — one for each agent. This is free and takes about 10 minutes total.

## Install Telegram

- **Phone:** Download Telegram from the App Store or Google Play.
- **Desktop:** Download from [telegram.org/apps](https://telegram.org/apps) (Windows, Mac, Linux).
- **Browser:** Use [web.telegram.org](https://web.telegram.org).

Create a Telegram account if you do not have one (a phone number is required for registration).

## Create Bots Using @BotFather

BotFather is Telegram's official bot creation service. It has a blue verified checkmark.

1. In Telegram, search for **@BotFather** and open a chat.
2. Send the command `/newbot` and follow the prompts:
   - **Name:** A human-readable display name (e.g., `Henry ClawBot`)
   - **Username:** A unique handle ending in `bot` (e.g., `henryclawbot` — must be globally unique, so add your initials if taken)
3. BotFather responds with a **token** that looks like this:
   ```
   8732631641:AAHu1OuUh8uRXqpZqH_6G77DMOwIAXVaRKU
   ```
4. Repeat `/newbot` for all 5 bots:

| Display Name | Suggested Username | Agent | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| Henry ClawBot | `henryclawbot` | henry | Chief of Staff — strategy and delegation |
| Coder ClawBot | `coderclawbot` | coder | Developer — code, data analysis |
| Scout ClawBot | `scoutclawbot` | scout | Researcher — web search, trend monitoring |
| Writer ClawBot | `writerclawbot` | writer | Content creator — memos and reports |
| Watcher ClawBot | `watcherclawbot` | watcher | System monitor — health and diagnostics |

> **Save all 5 tokens in a text file on your computer before continuing.** You cannot retrieve tokens from BotFather again (though you can generate a new one with `/token` if needed).

> **Tip:** To make a second bot, just send `/newbot` to the same BotFather chat again. No need to start over.

---

# Part 3: Get Your Anthropic API Key

Your agents run on Claude language models hosted by Anthropic. You need an API key to authenticate.

1. Go to [console.anthropic.com](https://console.anthropic.com) and create an account (or log in).
2. Navigate to **API Keys** in the left sidebar.
3. Click **Create Key**, name it `ClawInc`, and copy the key immediately.
   - Keys begin with `sk-ant-api03-...`
   - **You can only view the key once.** Copy it to your text file now.
4. Add a payment method if prompted. Anthropic requires this to activate API access.

> **Cost estimate:** For a typical class project with moderate agent activity, expect **\$5–\$20/month** in API charges. Henry (Opus 4.6) is the most expensive per call; Watcher and Scout (Haiku 4.5) are inexpensive. Your cron schedule largely determines your bill.

---

# Part 3b: Create Your Discord Webhook

All agent reports are automatically delivered to a Discord server channel. You need one **webhook URL** — a single URL that all 5 agents post to, each signing their messages with their own name and color.

## Step 1 — Create a Discord Account and Server

1. Go to [discord.com](https://discord.com) and sign in, or create a free account.
2. In the left sidebar, click the large **+** button at the bottom (Add a Server).
3. Choose **Create My Own** → **For me and my friends**.
4. Give it a name like `ClawInc` and click **Create**.

## Step 2 — Create a Text Channel Called #reports

1. In your new server, look at the left sidebar. You will see **TEXT CHANNELS** as a heading.
2. Hover your mouse over the words **TEXT CHANNELS** — a small **+** icon appears to the right.
3. Click the **+** icon.
4. Leave the type as **Text Channel**.
5. Type `reports` as the channel name.
6. Click **Create Channel**.

You now have a `#reports` channel in your server.

## Step 3 — Create the Webhook

1. Click your **server name** at the very top of the left sidebar.
2. Choose **Server Settings** from the dropdown menu.
3. In the left menu of Server Settings, click **Integrations**.
4. Click **Webhooks** → then click **New Webhook**.
5. Give it a name: `ClawInc Reports`.
6. Click the **Channel** dropdown and select `#reports`.
7. Click **Copy Webhook URL**.

The URL you just copied looks like this:
```
https://discord.com/api/webhooks/1234567890123456789/xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx
```

**That entire URL is your webhook.** There is no separate ID or token to find — just copy and paste the whole URL. Save it somewhere — you will paste it into the deploy script in the next step.

> **One webhook is all you need.** All 5 agents post to the same `#reports` channel. Each agent signs their message with their own name and color: Henry in gold, Scout in green, Writer in purple, Coder in blue, Watcher in orange.

# Part 4: Deploy ClawInc on Your Server

## Upload the Deploy Package

The `deploy/` folder in this repository contains everything needed to install and configure ClawInc. Copy it to your server from your **local computer** (not from the server terminal):

**Mac/Linux:**
```bash
scp -r deploy/ root@YOUR_DROPLET_IP:/root/deploy/
```

**Windows (Command Prompt or PowerShell):**
```bash
scp -r deploy/ root@YOUR_DROPLET_IP:/root/deploy/
```

**Windows — WinSCP (graphical alternative):**

If `scp` does not work on your Windows machine, use [WinSCP](https://winscp.net) (free):

1. Open WinSCP. Set Protocol to **SCP**.
2. Host name: your droplet IP. Username: `root`. Password: your root password.
3. Click **Login**, navigate to `/root/` on the server side.
4. Drag the `deploy/` folder from your computer into the `/root/` directory on the server.

## Edit the Deploy Script

Before running the script, you must insert your own credentials. On your **server terminal**:

```bash
nano /root/deploy/deploy-openclaw.sh
```

The top of the file has a configuration block. Fill in all 6 values:

```bash
# ============================================================
# CONFIGURATION — EDIT THESE BEFORE RUNNING
# ============================================================

ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="sk-ant-api03-YOUR-KEY-HERE"

TELEGRAM_TOKEN_HENRY="YOUR_HENRY_BOT_TOKEN"
TELEGRAM_TOKEN_CODER="YOUR_CODER_BOT_TOKEN"
TELEGRAM_TOKEN_SCOUT="YOUR_SCOUT_BOT_TOKEN"
TELEGRAM_TOKEN_WRITER="YOUR_WRITER_BOT_TOKEN"
TELEGRAM_TOKEN_WATCHER="YOUR_WATCHER_BOT_TOKEN"
DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL="https://discord.com/api/webhooks/paste-your-full-webhook-url-here"
```

> **Paste the entire webhook URL** you copied from Discord Server Settings → Integrations → Webhooks. Do not try to split it into an ID and token — just paste the whole URL between the quotes.

> **v0.90 note:** There are now **5 bot token variables** and a **Discord webhook URL**. Fill in all of them before running the script.

Save and exit nano: press `Ctrl+X`, then `Y`, then `Enter`.

## Run the Deploy Script

Make the script executable and run it:

```bash
chmod +x /root/deploy/deploy-openclaw.sh
/root/deploy/deploy-openclaw.sh
```

The script runs for **10–15 minutes** and performs the following phases automatically:

| Phase | What happens |
|-------|-------------|
| **System prep** | Updates Ubuntu packages, creates 2 GB swap file (critical for 1 GB RAM servers) |
| **Node.js install** | Installs Node.js 24 via NodeSource |
| **OpenClaw install** | Installs OpenClaw 2026.3.31 from npm globally |
| **User setup** | Creates `clawuser` system account, sets up workspace directories |
| **Config generation** | Writes `openclaw.json` with your API key, all 5 agent definitions, and all 5 bot bindings |
| **Firewall** | Opens ports 22 (SSH), 8050 (dashboard), and blocks everything else |
| **Service install** | Installs and starts the `openclaw` systemd service |
| **Dashboard install** | Installs Python dashboard dependencies, installs and starts `clawinc-dashboard` systemd service on port 8050 |

Watch the output scroll by. Successful completion is indicated by a green summary at the end.

## Add the 6 Cron Jobs

After the script finishes, add the automated daily schedule. Run this block in its entirety:

```bash
su - clawuser << 'CRONEOF'

openclaw cron add \
  --name "morning-research" --agent "scout" \
  --cron "0 8 * * *" --session isolated \
  --message "Run your morning research routine. Search the web for the latest trending topics in AI, marketing analytics, and technology. Focus on developments from the last 24 hours. Write a structured briefing with key findings, notable trends, and actionable insights. Save the briefing to your memory. Then post a signed summary to the Discord guild using your discord-report skill."

openclaw cron add \
  --name "daily-memo" --agent "writer" \
  --cron "0 9 * * *" --session isolated \
  --message "Compile the morning memo. Search Scout memory for today's research briefing. Synthesize into a polished executive memo with sections: Top Stories, Trend Analysis, Action Items, Market Watch. Save to your memory. Then post the full memo to the Discord guild using your discord-report skill, signed as Writer."

openclaw cron add \
  --name "overnight-worker" --agent "coder" \
  --cron "0 2 * * *" --session isolated \
  --message "Check your task queue and Henry's recent delegations. Work on the highest-priority pending development task. If no tasks are queued, review code for improvements and document any technical debt found. Post a summary of what was completed to the Discord guild using your discord-report skill, signed as Coder."

openclaw cron add \
  --name "health-check" --agent "watcher" \
  --cron "*/30 * * * *" --session isolated \
  --message "Check system resources: CPU, RAM, disk, and swap usage. Verify all agents are responsive. Review error logs from the past 30 minutes. Only post to the Discord guild (using your discord-report skill) if a metric exceeds warning thresholds or an error is found — do not post routine all-clear messages."

openclaw cron add \
  --name "nightly-rnd" --agent "henry" \
  --cron "0 23 * * *" --session isolated \
  --message "Initiate the nightly R&D session. Review today's memo from Writer, research from Scout, and any code from Coder. Identify strategic opportunities and improvements. Delegate follow-up tasks to team members as appropriate. Post a summary of tonight's R&D findings and delegations to the Discord guild using your discord-report skill, signed as Henry."

openclaw cron add \
  --name "session-cleanup" --agent "watcher" \
  --cron "0 4 * * 0" --session isolated \
  --message "Perform weekly session cleanup. Archive sessions older than 7 days. Remove temporary files. Post a cleanup summary (storage freed, any anomalies) to the Discord guild using your discord-report skill, signed as Watcher."

openclaw cron list
CRONEOF
```

The final command prints a table confirming all 6 jobs are registered.

# Part 4b: Adding Discord to an Already-Running Server

If you already ran the deploy script and want to add Discord now, do this on your server (no re-deployment needed):

```bash
nano /home/clawuser/.openclaw/openclaw.json
```

Find the `"env"` section near the top. It currently looks like:

```json
"env": {
    "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY": "sk-ant-api03-..."
},
```

Add a comma after the API key line and add the Discord webhook URL on the next line:

```json
"env": {
    "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY": "sk-ant-api03-...",
    "DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL": "https://discord.com/api/webhooks/paste-your-full-url-here"
},
```

Save: press `Ctrl+X` → `Y` → `Enter`. Then restart:

```bash
systemctl restart openclaw
```

> **The webhook URL goes between the quotes exactly as you copied it from Discord.** It is one long URL — do not split it or change it.

# Part 5: Verify Everything Is Working

## Check the Gateway Service

On your server, confirm the main OpenClaw service is running:

```bash
systemctl status openclaw
```

Look for `Active: active (running)`. If it shows `failed` or `inactive`, jump to Part 10 (Troubleshooting).

```bash
systemctl status clawinc-dashboard
```

This confirms the Shiny dashboard service is also running on port 8050.

## Check Agent Status via CLI

```bash
su - clawuser -c "openclaw status"
```

Expected output includes:
- **Gateway:** `reachable`
- **Agents:** `5`
- **Channels:** lists all 5 Telegram bot connections

```bash
su - clawuser -c "openclaw agents list --bindings"
```

This prints a table of all 5 agents with their assigned Telegram bot usernames. Confirm all 5 rows appear and show `bound`.

## Test All 5 Bots in Telegram

1. Open Telegram and search for your Henry bot by username (e.g., `@henryclawbot`).
2. Press **Start** or send `/start`.
3. Send a message:
   ```
   Hello! Who are you and what can you do?
   ```
4. Henry should respond within a few seconds. He is powered by Claude Opus 4.6 and will introduce himself and describe his capabilities.

Repeat this test for all 5 bots: Coder, Scout, Writer, and Watcher.

> **If a bot does not respond:** Do not panic. See Part 10. The most common causes are a typo in the token or the service not yet fully started. Give it 60 seconds and try again.

## Open the Dashboard

In your browser, go to:

```
http://YOUR_DROPLET_IP:8050
```

You should see the ClawInc monitoring dashboard. If it loads, your deployment is complete.

# Part 6: The Monitoring Dashboard

## Accessing the Dashboard

The v0.78 dashboard runs as a public service on port 8050. There is no SSH tunnel required — open your browser and navigate directly to:

```
http://YOUR_DROPLET_IP:8050
```

Bookmark this URL. You can share it with your project partners so everyone on your team can monitor the agents without needing server access.

> **Security note:** The dashboard is read-only. It displays information but cannot issue commands to agents. There is no risk of someone using it to control your system.

## What the Dashboard Shows

The dashboard refreshes automatically every **30 seconds**. It is organized into the following panels:

| Panel | Content |
|-------|---------|
| **System Metrics** | CPU usage, RAM usage, swap usage, disk usage — with color-coded status indicators |
| **Agent Cards** | One card per agent showing name, model, Telegram bot username, and last activity time |
| **Telegram Bot Status** | Live connection check for all 5 bots — green (connected) or red (disconnected) |
| **Cron Jobs** | All 6 scheduled tasks with next-run times and last-run status |
| **Activity Log** | Rolling list of recent agent actions, messages received, and system events |

## Dashboard Limitations

The dashboard is a **monitoring tool only**. You cannot send messages to agents, change configuration, or restart services from it. All commands go through Telegram or the server terminal.

# Part 7: Customizing Your Agents

## Editing an Agent's Personality (SOUL.md)

Each agent's behavior is defined by its `SOUL.md` file — a system prompt written in plain Markdown. To customize Henry's personality:

```bash
nano /home/clawuser/.openclaw/workspace-henry/SOUL.md
```

You can change:
- The agent's name and how it refers to itself
- Its stated role and areas of expertise
- Its communication style (formal, casual, concise, detailed)
- Its decision-making principles
- Any standing instructions (e.g., "always include citations" or "keep responses under 200 words")

After editing, restart the gateway to apply changes:

```bash
systemctl restart openclaw
```

The other agents' SOUL files are at:
```
/home/clawuser/.openclaw/workspace-coder/SOUL.md
/home/clawuser/.openclaw/workspace-scout/SOUL.md
/home/clawuser/.openclaw/workspace-writer/SOUL.md
/home/clawuser/.openclaw/workspace-watcher/SOUL.md
```

## Changing Agent Models

To change which Claude model an agent uses, edit the main config file:

```bash
nano /home/clawuser/.openclaw/openclaw.json
```

Find the agent entry and change the `model` field. Available models:

| Model ID | Speed | Capability | Cost per call |
|----------|-------|-----------|---------------|
| `anthropic/claude-opus-4-6` | Slower | Highest reasoning | High |
| `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929` | Medium | Strong all-around | Medium |
| `anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` | Fast | Efficient for simple tasks | Low |

After editing, validate and restart:

```bash
su - clawuser -c "openclaw config validate"
systemctl restart openclaw
```

## Adding Skills

Skills are pre-built task templates stored as Markdown files in each agent's `skills/` directory. A skill is triggered by a `/skill-name` command in Telegram.

To list Scout's existing skills:

```bash
ls /home/clawuser/.openclaw/workspace-scout/skills/
```

To create a new skill, add a `.md` file with the trigger name and a task template. For example, a `competitor-analysis` skill for Scout would automatically follow a structured competitive research framework whenever you send `/competitor-analysis` to the Scout bot.

# Part 8: Using Your Agents for the Class Project

## Sending Commands via Telegram

Send messages directly to any bot. Be specific about what you want. The agents understand natural language, but clear instructions produce better results.

**Henry (Chief of Staff — use for complex, multi-step tasks):**
```
Research the top 3 trends in social media marketing in Q1 2026.
Have Scout do a deep web search, then have Writer produce a
2-page executive brief. Send it to me when complete.
```

**Scout (Research — use for web search and information gathering):**
```
Find 5 recent academic papers on AI-driven customer segmentation
published since January 2025. Summarize each with key findings
and a citation.
```

**Coder (Developer — use for data analysis, scripting, and technical work):**
```
I have a CSV of customer purchase data. Write a Python script
to run a logistic regression predicting repeat purchase.
Show me the output and explain the key coefficients.
```

**Writer (Content — use for polished written deliverables):**
```
Write a 500-word executive summary of our Q1 marketing strategy.
Use formal business style. Include an abstract, 3 key findings,
and 2 specific recommendations.
```

**Watcher (System Monitor — use for server diagnostics):**
```
Run a full system health check. Report RAM, disk, swap,
and CPU usage. Tell me if anything looks abnormal.
```

## Voice Messages

Telegram supports voice notes on mobile. Record a voice note and send it to any bot — OpenClaw transcribes the audio and processes it as a text message. This is convenient for quick commands when you are away from a keyboard.

## Searching Agent Memory

Agents store information from past conversations and cron runs in their memory. To search what Scout has saved:

```bash
su - clawuser -c "openclaw memory search 'marketing trends' --agent scout"
```

Replace `scout` with any agent name and update the search query as needed.

## Watching Activity in Real Time

To see what your agents are doing right now:

```bash
journalctl -u openclaw -f
```

Press `Ctrl+C` to stop the live log. You can also watch this in the dashboard's Activity Log panel.

# Part 9: Useful Commands Reference

## Server Management

```bash
# Check if the OpenClaw gateway is running
systemctl is-active openclaw

# Start the gateway
systemctl start openclaw

# Stop the gateway
systemctl stop openclaw

# Restart (apply config changes)
systemctl restart openclaw

# View live gateway logs
journalctl -u openclaw -f

# View last 50 log lines (no pager)
journalctl -u openclaw -n 50 --no-pager

# Check the dashboard service
systemctl status clawinc-dashboard

# Restart the dashboard service
systemctl restart clawinc-dashboard

# Check RAM and swap
free -h

# Check disk space
df -h /

# Check CPU and memory usage interactively
top
```

## OpenClaw CLI (run as clawuser)

Switch to the clawuser account once, then run multiple commands:

```bash
su - clawuser
openclaw status
openclaw agents list --bindings
openclaw cron list
exit
```

Or run individual commands as root without switching accounts:

```bash
# Check overall gateway status
su - clawuser -c "openclaw status"

# List all agents with Telegram bot bindings
su - clawuser -c "openclaw agents list --bindings"

# List all scheduled cron jobs
su - clawuser -c "openclaw cron list"

# Manually trigger a cron job (useful for testing)
su - clawuser -c "openclaw cron run morning-research"

# Search agent memory
su - clawuser -c "openclaw memory search 'query text' --agent scout"

# Test Telegram bot connections
su - clawuser -c "openclaw channels status --probe"

# Run system diagnostics
su - clawuser -c "openclaw doctor"

# Validate the config file
su - clawuser -c "openclaw config validate"
```

## Dashboard and Config

```bash
# Check if dashboard is accessible (run on server)
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://localhost:8050

# Edit the main config file
nano /home/clawuser/.openclaw/openclaw.json

# After editing, validate before restarting
su - clawuser -c "openclaw config validate"
systemctl restart openclaw
```

# Part 10: Troubleshooting

## Bot Not Responding

**Symptoms:** You send a message to a bot and receive no reply after 30 seconds.

**Steps:**

1. Check that the service is running:
   ```bash
   systemctl is-active openclaw
   ```
2. If it is not active, check why:
   ```bash
   journalctl -u openclaw -n 30 --no-pager
   ```
3. Test the Telegram connections:
   ```bash
   su - clawuser -c "openclaw channels status --probe"
   ```
4. Verify the bot token in your config matches what BotFather gave you — even a single extra space will cause authentication failure:
   ```bash
   nano /home/clawuser/.openclaw/openclaw.json
   ```
5. Restart and test again:
   ```bash
   systemctl restart openclaw
   ```

## Config File Invalid

**Symptoms:** `openclaw config validate` prints errors; service fails to start.

**Diagnosis:**
```bash
su - clawuser -c "openclaw config validate"
```

**Common causes:**
- Trailing comma after the last item in a JSON array or object (JSON does not allow this)
- Mismatched brackets or braces
- Bot token left as the placeholder text (`YOUR_HENRY_BOT_TOKEN`)
- `dmPolicy: "open"` requires `allowFrom: ["*"]` to be set

Fix the JSON, validate again, then restart.

## Dashboard Not Loading

**Symptoms:** Browser shows connection refused or times out at `http://YOUR_IP:8050`.

**Steps:**

1. Check the dashboard service is running:
   ```bash
   systemctl status clawinc-dashboard
   ```
2. If it failed, view the error:
   ```bash
   journalctl -u clawinc-dashboard -n 30 --no-pager
   ```
3. Confirm port 8050 is open in the firewall:
   ```bash
   ufw status
   ```
   You should see `8050` listed as `ALLOW`. If not, add it:
   ```bash
   ufw allow 8050/tcp
   ```
4. Restart the dashboard service:
   ```bash
   systemctl restart clawinc-dashboard
   ```
5. Wait 10 seconds and reload the browser page.

## Gateway Not Starting

**Symptoms:** `systemctl start openclaw` runs but the service immediately stops.

**Diagnosis:**
```bash
journalctl -u openclaw -n 50 --no-pager
```

**Try running the gateway manually** to see the full error in real time:
```bash
su - clawuser -c "openclaw gateway run"
```

**Common causes:**
- Port 18789 (internal gateway port) is already in use by another process
- The config file has a syntax error (always validate before restarting)
- Node.js not found — confirm with `node --version`

## Out of Memory / Server Slow

**Symptoms:** Commands are sluggish; agents take a long time to respond; logs show OOM (out of memory) errors.

**Check memory:**
```bash
free -h
```

The `Swap` row should show approximately `2.0G total`. If swap shows `0`, the swapfile was not created or was lost after a reboot. Recreate it:

```bash
fallocate -l 2G /swapfile
chmod 600 /swapfile
mkswap /swapfile
swapon /swapfile
echo '/swapfile none swap sw 0 0' >> /etc/fstab
```

The `/etc/fstab` line ensures swap is remounted automatically on reboot.

## Lost Root Password

In the DigitalOcean dashboard, click your droplet name → **Access → Reset Root Password**. DigitalOcean will email a new temporary password.

# Appendix A: Quick-Start Checklist

Use this checklist to track your setup. All 14 items must be checked before your deployment is considered complete.

- [ ] Created DigitalOcean account and provisioned a droplet (Ubuntu 24.04, \$6/mo plan)
- [ ] Recorded my droplet IP address: `________________`
- [ ] Can connect to server via SSH (`ssh root@YOUR_IP`)
- [ ] Installed Telegram on phone and/or desktop
- [ ] Created all 5 bots via @BotFather: Henry, Coder, Scout, Writer, Watcher
- [ ] Saved all 5 bot tokens in a secure text file
- [ ] Created Anthropic API key at console.anthropic.com and saved it
- [ ] Uploaded the `deploy/` folder to `/root/deploy/` on the server
- [ ] Edited `deploy-openclaw.sh` with my Anthropic API key and all 5 bot tokens
- [ ] Ran the deploy script to completion with no fatal errors
- [ ] Config validates successfully: `openclaw config validate` returns **Config valid**
- [ ] Service is active: `systemctl is-active openclaw` returns **active**
- [ ] All 5 bots respond in Telegram (Henry, Coder, Scout, Writer, Watcher)
- [ ] Dashboard is accessible at `http://YOUR_IP:8050` in a browser
- [ ] All 6 cron jobs are listed in `openclaw cron list`

# Appendix B: Agent Roster

| Agent | Default Bot Username | Model | Primary Uses |
|-------|---------------------|-------|-------------|
| **Henry** | `@henryclawbot` | Claude Opus 4.6 | Strategic planning, task delegation, multi-agent coordination |
| **Coder** | `@coderclawbot` | Claude Sonnet 4.5 | Python/R scripting, data analysis, debugging, automation |
| **Scout** | `@scoutclawbot` | Claude Haiku 4.5 | Web research, news monitoring, competitive intelligence |
| **Writer** | `@writerclawbot` | Claude Sonnet 4.5 | Executive memos, reports, summaries, marketing copy |
| **Watcher** | `@watcherclawbot` | Claude Haiku 4.5 | System health monitoring, log analysis, resource alerts |

**Notes:**

- All 5 agents have Telegram bots as of v0.78. Watcher was previously headless (background-only).
- Bot usernames shown above are the defaults suggested in Part 2. Your actual usernames depend on what you chose when creating bots with BotFather.
- Models shown are the defaults. You can change any agent's model in `openclaw.json` (see Part 7).
- Henry (Opus 4.6) is the most capable and most expensive model. Direct complex, high-stakes tasks to Henry. Use Haiku-powered agents (Scout, Watcher) for high-frequency, routine tasks to keep API costs down.

# Appendix C: Cron Schedule Reference

All times are server time (UTC by default). If your server is in a US region, UTC is 5–6 hours ahead of Central Time.

| Cron Expression | Agent | Job Name | Task |
|----------------|-------|----------|------|
| `*/30 * * * *` | Watcher | `health-check` | System resource check every 30 minutes |
| `0 8 * * *` | Scout | `morning-research` | Daily web research scan at 8:00 AM |
| `0 9 * * *` | Writer | `daily-memo` | Compile morning intelligence memo at 9:00 AM |
| `0 23 * * *` | Henry | `nightly-rnd` | Nightly R&D strategy session at 11:00 PM |
| `0 2 * * *` | Coder | `overnight-worker` | Work on queued development tasks at 2:00 AM |
| `0 4 * * 0` | Watcher | `session-cleanup` | Weekly session archiving, Sundays at 4:00 AM |

To view the current schedule at any time:
```bash
su - clawuser -c "openclaw cron list"
```

To manually trigger any job for testing:
```bash
su - clawuser -c "openclaw cron run health-check"
```
